extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark for college-level multi-discipline multimodal understanding and reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks across six disciplines, covering 30 subjects, 183 subfields, and 30 heterogeneous image types to evaluate expert-level perception, knowledge, and reasoning in multimodal models.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue; Yuansheng Ni; Kai Zhang; Tianyu Zheng; Ruoqi Liu; Ge Zhang; Samuel Stevens; Dongfu Jiang; Weiming Ren; Yuxuan Sun; Cong Wei; Botao Yu; Ruibin Yuan; Renliang Sun; Ming Yin; Boyuan Zheng; Zhenzhu Yang; Yibo Liu; Wenhao Huang; Huan Sun; Yu Su; Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, and Wenhu Chen. MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv:2311.16502, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was manually collected in three stages: the authors selected 30 subjects across six disciplines, recruited over 50 university students including co-authors to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources and create new questions where necessary, and assembled a diverse collection that was later cleaned and filtered.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions sourced from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks; major textbooks and online resources; free online resources, quizzes, textbooks, and other study materials; lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the selected majors were recruited as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary; annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, select questions without immediately available answers, ensure all questions contain one or more images, are written in English, meet college-level difficulty, are unambiguous, and annotate fields including question, answer options, correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation; suspected duplicates were reviewed by the authors, problems were checked for format and typos, and authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels, excluding about 10% classified as very easy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: JSON file format; user-friendly web interface for data annotation and verification
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by the authors to eliminate duplications; problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking; authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels and excluded approximately 10% classified as very easy; a secondary review team rigorously vetted annotations and regular audits of random samples were conducted.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: over 50 university students specializing in these majors; 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and “90th percentile of skilled adults,” nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle; the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Level 3, or Expert AGI, marks a critical milestone... leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption; We believe MMMU will stimulate the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The annotators should avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning; measure three essential skills in LMMs: perception, knowledge, and reasoning; useful for hyperparameter selection
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Version Change Log documents updates from V1 to V4, including added model results, corrected typos, updated names, adjusted tables, and removal of an erroneous biology case.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, are excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking. This step requires authors to ensure adherence to a standardized format, undertaking necessary corrections where deviations are found.
